itemB: White TPO/PVC single-ply membrane — reflectance lever

verdict.winner: Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) leads on total NJ energy performance via added R-value; white TPO/PVC membranes lead on low-slope reflectance, per SPFA and the CRRC.
verdict.reasoning: Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) ranks first because it is the only covering here that adds conductive insulation — an aged R-6.0 to R-6.5 per inch, per ICC-ES/ASTM C1289 LTTR and SPFA — addressing Newark's heating-dominated Climate Zone 4A–5, where R-value governs winter heat loss, per the DOE.
verdict.alternate: White single-ply membrane (TPO/PVC) leads for low-slope cooling — its ~0.70–0.85 solar reflectance (ASTM C1549, CRRC) cuts peak summer cooling demand 11–27% in air-conditioned residential buildings, per the EPA, while cool-roof asphalt shingles carry CRRC-rated reflective granules as the lower-cost steep-slope path.

keyFacts: Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) carries an aged R-6.0 to R-6.5 per inch and is the only covering compared that adds conductive insulation, per ICC-ES/ASTM C1289 LTTR listings and SPFA.
White single-ply membrane (TPO and PVC) holds ~0.70–0.85 solar reflectance and ~0.80–0.90 thermal emittance, measured by ASTM C1549 and listed by the CRRC.
White PVC membrane holds the same ~0.70–0.85 reflectance band as white TPO plus chemical and grease resistance, suiting flat roofs near kitchen/grease exhaust, per the CRRC and Duro-Last.
Reflective metal roofing carries high solar reflectance and thermal emittance the CRRC rates, but no metal-specific reflectance percentage is sourced.
Cool-roof asphalt shingles use reflective granules to raise surface reflectance as a lower-cost steep-slope reflectance upgrade, and are CRRC-rated.
A green (vegetated) roof adds a planted layer rated only for a 5–40-year service life per the InterNACHI chart, with no sourced energy percentage.
Natural slate is a dense stone covering with no sourced cool-roof reflectance figure; it is a durable steep-slope covering, not a reflectance lever.
The SPF foam layer lasts 30+ years when its protective coating is maintained, per SPFA.
Reflective coatings and membranes add no conductive R-value; their energy effect comes only from solar reflectance and thermal emittance, per the DOE, CRRC, and RCMA.
White single-ply membrane (TPO/PVC) reduces peak summer cooling demand 11–27% in air-conditioned residential buildings, per the EPA.
A reflective roof stays over 50°F cooler than a conventional roof on a sunny afternoon, per the DOE and the LBNL Heat Island Group.
A clean white roof reflecting 80% of sunlight stays about 55°F (31°C) cooler than a gray roof reflecting 20%, per the DOE and the LBNL Heat Island Group.
Solar reflectance is the fraction of sunlight reflected and thermal emittance is how efficiently a surface re-radiates absorbed heat, each on a 0–1 scale, per the EPA.

The CRRC-1 program (Cool Roof Rating Council) is the active third-party rating system for roof reflectance and emittance, listing initial and 3-year-aged solar reflectance and thermal emittance in a public Rated Products Directory; it reports performance only, not an approval, per the CRRC.
The EPA ended ENERGY STAR roof program recognition on June 1, 2022, per the EPA, CRRC, and SPRI.
SPF is rated as an insulation lever (aged R-6.0–R-6.5/inch per ICC-ES and ASTM C1289 LTTR), while reflective coverings are rated on CRRC reflectance-and-emittance metrics, per SPFA and the CRRC.
NJ's Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) program pays a per-MWh SREC-II set by the NJ Board of Public Utilities over a 15-year term, per the NJBPU.

Solar-generating roofs draw NJ's sales-and-use-tax exemption on solar equipment (N.J.S.A. 54:32B-8.33) and a property-tax exemption on the added assessed value (N.J.S.A. 54:4-3.113a/b), each claimed on the homeowner's own filing, per the NJ Division of Taxation.
The federal residential §25D solar credit was 30% for systems completed through 2025 and was repealed for systems completed after December 31, 2025, per the IRS.
The federal §25C insulation credit was repealed after December 31, 2025, so no current federal homeowner credit applies to a cool or insulated roof, per the IRS.
Federal §179D is a commercial whole-building deduction (envelope, HVAC, lighting), not a standalone roof credit, and was repealed for construction beginning after June 30, 2026, per the IRS.

LBNL Heat Island Group (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)

njContext: Newark sits in Climate Zone 4A–5, a heating-dominated mixed climate, so total annual energy performance favors insulation levers — a reflective roof reduces peak summer cooling but carries a winter heating penalty, per the DOE and EPA.

The 2021 IECC (NJ-adopted, residential enforcement April 2023) sets ceiling insulation at R-60 for NJ's Climate Zones 4 and 5 under Table R402.1.3, with an R-49 full-ceiling exception at raised-heel eaves, per the ICC and NJ DCA; this conductive minimum applies regardless of the covering's reflectance.

Balanced attic ventilation supports any roof's energy performance — IRC R806.2 sets the minimum net free ventilating area at 1/150 of the vented attic (the 1/300 reduction's cold-zone vapor-retarder leg does not apply in Newark's Zone 4–5), split roughly 50% intake at the soffits and 50% exhaust at the ridge, per the IRC, ARMA, and Air Vent Inc.

For most Essex County houses on a roof replacement, cool-roof asphalt shingles raise surface reflectance at standard steep-slope shingle pricing and carry CRRC reflectance-and-emittance ratings; once ceiling insulation meets the 2021 IECC R-60 (R-49 raised-heel exception), reflectance adds only incremental summer benefit, per the CRRC and ICC.

Reflective metal roofing suits Essex County steep-slope homes seeking a rated reflective finish; green (vegetated) roofs fit limited flat residential sections, rated by InterNACHI only for a 5–40-year service life with no sourced energy percentage.

On low-slope commercial roofs, SPF adds the only conductive R-value (aged R-6.0–R-6.5/inch per SPFA) where a flat roof carries thin existing insulation, while white TPO/PVC's ~0.70–0.85 reflectance lowers roof-surface temperature, per the CRRC and EPA.

White PVC membrane suits commercial buildings near grease or chemical exhaust, holding the same ~0.70–0.85 reflectance band as white TPO plus chemical and grease resistance, per the CRRC and Duro-Last.
positioning: Position Newark Quality Roofing as a registered New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor (N.J.S.A. 56:8-136), insured, offering a free written estimate — NJ issues no roofing 'license,' so never claim a license. NQR installs both reflectance-lever coverings (white TPO/PVC, cool-roof asphalt shingles, reflective metal) and insulation-lever systems (SPF, above-deck/attic insulation) and can match the covering to Newark's heating-dominated Climate Zone 4A–5. For any solar-generating roof, NQR handles the roofing side only — mount flashing, ASCE 7 load, re-roof-before-solar sequencing, and NEC-fire/setback coordination — not the solar system design, sizing, or incentive filing (the homeowner's tax professional confirms §25D/§25C/SuSI eligibility). Frame warranty honestly as two parts: the manufacturer's material warranty plus NQR's written workmanship warranty; never invoke manufacturer certification tiers (no Master Elite / SELECT ShingleMaster framing) and never claim measured energy-savings percentages for NQR's own projects.
